text: Hey, come on in! Name's Shorty. The board member who never clocks out.
Watch this. The board uploads the rules, and boom, it's in my head.
Management, phone numbers, links, food truck night, bingo. All of it, straight in.
And now? I'm fully trained on your community. Any question, any hour, day or night. Twenty-four seven.
Eleven at night. Office is closed. Street's quiet.
But up in that house, a light's still on.
That's Sally. New puppy, no sleep, and a fence on her mind.
So she texts me. Right now. Eleven o'clock. And I answer instantly.
Zone two. Black aluminum, fifty-four inches max.
And here's the good part. A neighbor owns a fence company, so I offer to reach out.
She says yes. Just like that.
Done. Free estimate, tomorrow morning. Booked while she's in her pajamas.
Phone down. Puppy's curled up. Problem solved in thirty seconds.
Lights out. Sally sleeps. But me? I never do.
Now meet Betty. Seventy years young, and she lives for bingo.
Friday bingo is her whole week. But management emails? She never opens 'em.
And the gym, where they pin up the news? Betty doesn't go.
So she's missing everything. Bingo night, and she'd never know.
Until now. Right on her phone. Bingo night, fifteen spots left.
One tap, and she's in. Fourteen left!
Look at that face. Betty's happy, and bingo's saved.
She never had to open one single email.
Meanwhile, back at the office, I'm already hard at work.
Weekly newsletter? Typed, polished, sent to every resident.
Burn ban today? One text, and every phone lights up.
Resident reports? I read every single one. Streetlight out? Logged. Handled.
And look who rolled up outside the clubhouse. A food truck.
One tap on my phone, and lunch is ordered and paid.
Walk on out, and my food's already waiting for me.
Hot food. No waiting. No wallet. Just one tap.
And here's the thing. Sally and Betty? Not the only ones.
Every resident can do this. If a business is on the Shortlist...
...it's one tap, right in the app. Order lunch. Book the fence guy. Done.
Because this was never just about sending notices.
It's about making your community a great place to live.
That's Shorty, and the Shortlist.
